pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the samplers show about how far the spores carry from an infected stand?
settings: The catch falls away within a few hundred metres of an infected stand
The catch holds up across several kilometres of ground, thinning slowly with distance
The catch runs heaviest at middling distances, and thinner both close in and far out
The catch showed no steady relation to distance, tracking the height of the collector instead

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the orchard at Hedravean?
settings: It carries the fungus through repeated sprayings, a pressure the forest stands are spared
Its mapped and managed trees gave the team a known population to calibrate against
A long run of harvest records from it lets past outbreaks be given dates
Complaints from its growers were what first drew the team's attention to the fungus

pivots.stem: What is the professor's position on the claim that the fungus is spreading northward?
settings: She reads the apparent spread as a product of wider sampling, not of any shift in range
She credits it, chiefly because sites added in the north have begun to turn it up
She suspects the old southern finds were misnamed, and that the range was northern from the start

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the team will change in next season's survey?
settings: Keep collecting through the winter months instead of stopping in the autumn
Replace the sticky slides with a filter cartridge that a machine can read
Shift part of the effort from the interior of each plot toward its edges
Set a rain gauge beside each collector so catches can be read against the weather

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the ledger kept by the Trelundy infirmary's dispenser?
settings: Its running totals let historians work out how many beds the house actually kept filled
Marginal notes in it preserve queries the dispenser raised about dosages the prescribing physicians had set
It shows the practice cost enough that the governors debated giving it up more than once

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central point about the infirmary's weekly weighing of patients?
settings: It began as a check on the kitchen's provisioning and drifted into a diagnostic habit
Physicians read the charts as tracking recovery, while the ward staff had other ends in view

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did Maderwyn's re-examination of the weight registers find?
settings: Patients taken in over the winter gained at rates the summer intake did not approach
The recorded gains cluster at round figures, a sign readings were rounded before entry
Books kept by different attendants ran too nearly alike to be independent records

pivots.stem: What is the professor's view of Rostrellick's claim that the weighing shaped who was admitted?
settings: He accepts it, pointing to admission notes that discuss a candidate's likely response to the regimen
He rejects it, since admission rested with subscribers kept at arm's length from the data
He holds the surviving papers cannot settle it until the admission registers are worked through
He grants a narrower version, with the weighing shaping who was kept on rather than taken in

pivots.stem: What is the professor's main point about the survey of Lanmorick priory made in the 1840s?
settings: Its measurements follow the restorers' brief, recording what the planned works needed and little more
It deserves more trust than the drawings made from it, which tidied irregularities the field books preserve
Its lasting value lies in what it caught by accident, parts of the fabric lost soon afterward
It served as a training exercise, and its errors follow the order in which the pupils worked

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the laser scan show about the shape of the priory's tower?
settings: The tower leans by a small but consistent amount toward the southwest
The tower's cross-section is slightly oval rather than round, wider along the river face
Its upper stage sits slightly off the axis of the stages beneath it
Its courses undulate in a way consistent with ground movement while building was under way

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the recording team intends to do next?
settings: Extend the scanning into the roof spaces, which the first campaign left untouched
Put the scan through a structural model, to test what the tower can still safely carry
Repeat the scan after an interval long enough to test how repeatable its readings are
Move on to the parish's other early buildings to give the priory a comparison

pivots.stem: Why does the professor discuss the mason's marks in the priory's choir?
settings: Their placement lets the team assign stretches of walling to particular building seasons
They cluster where the fabric shows rebuilding, which helps put a date to the repairs
One of them recurs at a quarry the team recorded, tying the choir's stone to a source
Their spacing offers a check on the unit of length the medieval masons worked to

pivots.stem: What is the professor's position on Lensham's claim that the prefaces to each part were written to answer the reviewers?
settings: She agrees, matching several passages in them to notices that had appeared in the quarterlies
She disputes it, taking the prefaces to address the subscribers whose payments the parts depended on
She allows it from the middle parts onward, the earlier prefaces being pitched at the volunteer helpers
She takes their audience to have been the editorial staff, with reviewers answered by letter

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest scholars will be able to do once the project's archive is catalogued?
settings: Establish how the work was shared out, from the marks each editor left on the material
Recover entries written and then cut before the parts went to the printer
Date when particular senses first drew notice, from the postmarks the incoming packets carry

pivots.stem: Why does the professor dwell on the entry for a dialect name for a fishing float?
settings: Its evidence came from a single county, which forced a decision about regional labels
Its definition survives in six successive drafts, which show the house style taking shape
An error in its etymology outlived four printings, showing how slowly corrections spread

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the recount of the citation slips in the boxes show?
settings: Boxes for the commonest words had been thinned at some point, with the discards going unrecorded
The published counts overstate the holdings for the letters late in the alphabet
Material in the earliest hands sat misfiled under spellings a reform had since changed

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply about the team's plans for identifying individual salamanders?

pivots.stem: What did the professor say the recapture figures showed about the population estimate?
settings: Estimates from the spring sessions ran well above the autumn ones for the same reach

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central claim about what the long-running survey has measured?
settings: Less the population than a readiness to enter traps, which swings with the weather

Mostly the habits of the observers, whose favored stretches supply the bulk of the detections

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to Polgrenna's suggestion that the salamanders breed at a second, undiscovered site?
settings: He credits it, mainly because young turn up in the counts before eggs are seen locally
He thinks it may hold in wet years, while in dry ones the known pools suffice

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did records of a rival studio in the same town show about its pricing of portrait sittings?
settings: It charged a flat fee regardless of how many prints were ordered, unlike Morgelly's per-print scale
It kept single sittings level with Morgelly's rates but undercut him for group portraits
Its prices climbed each time a new photographic process reached the town, tracking material costs

pivots.stem: What is the professor's response to Chelvern's argument that the ledger was written up after the fact for advertisement?
settings: She rejects it, pointing to shifts of ink from entry to entry that fit a book kept daily
She accepts it, reading the uniform hand across the pages as a sign the book was copied out afterward for display

pivots.stem: Why does the professor set the ledger beside the price lists of the plate makers?
settings: To show the exposure figures shortening just as faster plates came onto the market

To argue that selling supplies on the side earned him more than the camera work did

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central point about what the ledger offers historians?
settings: It preserves one man's judgment of light, usable as an instrument once his habits are known

It registers the sitters as much as the light, since the settings shift with who sat

pivots.stem: Why does the professor describe the arrangements at the measured mile off Aberwynt?
settings: To bring out how much of its upkeep fell on the port authority instead of the navy

To identify the shore observers whose sightings produced the timings the navy released

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the newly catalogued papers from the builders' yard are likely to show?
settings: How far the marker posts had strayed from the distance the charts assigned them
Whether the Penvorran ran with her intended propellers or a set borrowed for the day
What the builders privately took the ship's draught to be on the morning in question

pivots.stem: Where does the professor stand on Nansveor's charge that trial speeds were inflated across the fleet?

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the survey of trial-day coal returns across the fleet show?
settings: Consumption varied more between stokehold crews than between the ships they served in

Ships tried in the winter months returned higher figures than those tried in summer

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the research group will do with the soundings series?

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central claim about what the silt record of the Marnstow estuary shows?

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did Ordwell's replotting of the old soundings reveal?

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the ferry slip at Fenrith?
